$description: Project Settings › Data Shapes: the project-level `$defs` editor. The left column lists the shapes and the right one edits the selected shape's fields, each field a name, a type, an optional format and whether it is required — plus the target of a reference and the children of an object. The adapter (`surfaces/settings-defs.ts`) hands in the shapes, the fields already classified, and every draft the reader is part-way through typing; `settings/defs-editor.ts` decides what a name may be and what reaches `project.json`. Nothing here reads the configuration: a document that re-read the file while drawing would be a second opinion about what one module already owns.

style.$description: What `.settings-two-col`, `.settings-list-panel`, `.settings-editor-panel`, `.settings-editor-header`, `.settings-empty-state`, `.settings-inline-form`, `.schema-field-list`, `.schema-field-card`, `.schema-field-row`, `.schema-field-nested`, `.schema-field-name-input`, `.schema-nested-add`, `.schema-add-field` and `.settings-section-title` said in `styles/overlays.css`, keyed on `part` and re-pointed at the studio token layer. NONE of those rules is deleted from the stylesheet: `settings/contributed-section.ts` draws the same two-column editor and `ui/form-controls.ts` draws the same field cards, both still lit, so this document carries its own copy of each until they convert. Two values could not come with them. `.settings-editor-header h3` read `var(--spectrum-font-size-100, 14px)` and `.schema-field-card--nested` read `var(--spectrum-gray-300, #444)`, and a document is mounted in the pane rather than inside `<sp-theme>`, so both would have taken their hard-coded fallback every time; they are the kit's `--jx-text-lg` and the studio layer's `--border`.

& [part=\"columns\"].$description: The 1px gap over the border colour is the divider between the two columns: two panels on `--bg-panel` with `--border` showing through the gap, so nothing draws a rule of its own.

& [part=\"shape\"] > [part=\"control\"],.$description: `.settings-list-panel sp-action-button` said `width: 100%; justify-content: flex-start`, and both halves belong to the button the row is made of rather than to the row: a kit action button centres its glyph and its label, which reads as a list of centred names.

& [part=\"field-label\"].$description: The field's name in words, which `.schema-field-label` named and no stylesheet ever styled: it was an `sp-field-label` beside the raw-key field, at whatever size Spectrum drew it. It is a caption on the row rather than a label for a control, so it says so in the type ramp and the dim colour instead of borrowing a control's typography.

empty.textContent: Pick a data shape on the left, or create one.

children.$description: Whether the shape requires this field. The word on screen is the name: `Req` is slotted rather than passed as `label`, because the kit's switch wraps its control in the label the slot lands in, and a second name would be announced over the top of it. Which row it belongs to is the tooltip's job instead, which is what `hint` is.

$props.label: Type of the new field in ${$map.item.label}
